business_scope.primary_industry_name: AI Video Synthesis and Virtual Avatar Generation Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income
Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the United States of America

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 288 through 328 (incorporation of a limited liability company, Yuhan Hoesa), Article 543 (board of directors), and Article 583 (application of provisions to limited liability companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (법원등기국) via the Korean Court Registration Information System (인터넷등기소), administered by the local district court having jurisdiction over the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서), filed with the competent district court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the paid-in capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation, and the amount must be deposited into a bank escrow account in the name of the company or its incorporators, with a certificate of deposit issued by the bank and submitted to the registry. The capital can be as low as KRW 1, but practical banking and licensing considerations may require a higher amount.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [DATE] with registration number [REGISTRATION NO.]; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all actions necessary to commence business operations, including the subscription of share capital, the establishment of banking relationships, the adoption of a registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire issued share capital of the Company, consisting of [NUMBER] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [PAR VALUE] each, for an aggregate consideration of KRW [TOTAL CAPITAL]. The Board confirms that all such shares have been fully paid in cash or in kind as per the subscription agreements, and that the statutory deposit requirement has been satisfied by the deposit of the full capital amount into the designated escrow account at [BANK NAME] under account number [ACCOUNT NO.]. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly or severally, to open, operate, and manage all corporate bank accounts, to execute all banking documents, to sign checks and wire transfer instructions, and to establish online banking credentials with any domestic or international financial institution, including but not limited to Stripe and Paddle payment gateways, for the purpose of receiving client payments and managing corporate funds. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board hereby adopts the registered office of the Company at [FULL ADDRESS], Republic of Korea, as the legal seat of the Company, and authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease or service agreements and to file all necessary notices with the Registry Office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer (대표이사), [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer (재무이사), and [NAME] as Auditor (감사), each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are duly elected. The Board authorizes the officers to represent the Company in all matters, to execute all contracts, and to comply with all statutory filing obligations. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer to take all further actions, execute all documents, and pay all fees necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including the registration of the Company with the National Tax Service, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and any other regulatory bodies. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the corporate records. ADOPTED this [DATE] by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors. /s/ [DIRECTOR NAME], /s/ [DIRECTOR NAME], /s/ [DIRECTOR NAME].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and Korean Court Registry Office (법원등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name (Yuhan Hoesa), purpose (AI video synthesis and virtual avatar generation software development, SaaS provision, and related consulting), registered office address, share capital, number of shares, and initial directors. The articles must be signed by all incorporators and notarized by a Korean notary public. The notarization fee is approximately KRW 50,000. After notarization, the articles are submitted to the registry office as part of the incorporation filing. Ensure that the company name is reserved via the name search system (상호검색) before notarization.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all incorporators (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if using an agent
Capital deposit certificate (자본금예치증명서) from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry office issues a query or suspension, review the notice for missing or incorrect information. Correct the articles or supplementary documents and resubmit within the given cure period (typically 2 weeks). If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and re-file. Engage a local legal counsel to expedite the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Escrow Account Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori) and the Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company or the incorporators at a Korean commercial bank. Deposit the full subscribed capital (minimum KRW 1, but recommended at least KRW 10,000,000 for operational credibility). Obtain a certificate of deposit (자본금예치증명서) from the bank, which must be submitted with the incorporation filing. The bank will verify the identity of the depositors and the source of funds. After the company is registered, the funds are released to the company's corporate account. Ensure the deposit is made within the statutory timeframe (typically before the incorporation filing).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit due to AML concerns, provide additional source-of-funds documentation (e.g., bank statements, tax returns). If the deposit certificate is delayed, request a provisional certificate or coordinate with the registry office for a conditional filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Court Registry Office (법원등기소) – Internet Registration Service (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application online or in person to the district court with jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, identification of directors and auditor, and the registration fee (approximately KRW 150,000). The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court issues a Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인등기사항증명서). This certificate is the legal proof of the company's existence. The registration must be completed within 2 weeks of the notarization of the articles.
required_dossiers: Consent forms from directors and auditor (if not incorporators)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a suspension or rejection, the applicant will receive a written notice specifying the defects. Correct the defects and resubmit within the statutory cure period (usually 2 weeks). If the issue is substantive (e.g., illegal purpose), amend the articles and re-notarize. Seek legal assistance to expedite the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Business Licensing Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean National Tax Service (국세청) and Local Tax Office (지방세청)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days of incorporation, register the company with the National Tax Service for corporate tax and VAT. Obtain a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local tax office. This certificate is required for opening corporate bank accounts, issuing tax invoices, and contracting with clients. Additionally, register for the four major social insurance schemes (national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, industrial accident insurance) at the relevant authorities. For a digital software company, no separate industrial license is required, but if the company engages in any physical activities, additional permits may be needed. The business registration application can be filed online via HomeTax (홈택스).
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business purpose or office address, provide additional documentation such as a detailed business plan or a revised lease agreement. If the registration is delayed, the company may still operate but must file taxes within the statutory deadlines. Seek a tax professional to resolve any issues.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS) (www.customs.go.kr) administers export declarations/customs clearances for export VAT substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Complete incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) under the Korean Commercial Act and obtain the court registration certificate. Step 2: Within 20 days from business commencement, file the statutory Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office or through HomeTax. Step 3: NTS issues a single 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number, VAT registration number, and e-Tax invoice identifier. Step 4: If Yuhan Hoesa were a foreign non-resident entity with no domestic place of business (not the case for this domestic LLC), it would be required to appoint a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes and use the simplified registration procedure for foreign electronic-service suppliers to obtain a foreign business operator registration number before charging Korean VAT. Step 5: Register for the HomeTax e-Tax invoice system and optionally enrol a certified electronic tax invoice API/ERP integration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or equivalent pass-through election for a Korean domestic limited liability company. Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a resident domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Act and as a VAT registrant under the Value-Added Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold for an incorporated Korean domestic business; VAT registration is mandatory from business commencement under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act. The KRW 80 million simplified-taxpayer threshold is available only to unincorporated individual entrepreneurs and is not available to Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign non-resident electronic-service suppliers also have no turnover threshold and must register if they supply digital services to Korean consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT registered businesses must issue an approved tax invoice. Electronic tax invoices (e-Tax invoices) are mandatory and must be transmitted to the NTS through HomeTax (or a certified ERP/API integration) by the day immediately following issuance. The NTS does not use real-time fiscal clearance digital stamping; it operates a centralized anti-fraud data-matching system, including e-Tax invoice cross-verification, cash receipt records, and foreign-exchange transaction matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of AI avatar video generation SaaS and related digital services to non-resident customers qualify for 0% VAT under Article 20(1) of the Value-Added Tax Act if the place of supply is outside Korea, the service is actually consumed or used outside Korea, the customer is a non-resident/non-domestic business, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency from abroad and repatriated to Korea. Pure software exports without physical goods must be supported by evidence of foreign consumption and foreign-exchange settlement; if any media is physically delivered, the goods must be exported through KCS and the export declaration must be retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Certificate (export acceptance) issued by Korea Customs Service, required for physical goods exports and for any physical media/mixed-supply delivery accompanying the software
Commercial invoice and master service agreement (or order/contract) with the named non-resident customer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill when physical media or tangible components are exported
Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate or Certificate of Receipt of Export Proceeds issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing inbound remittance from the non-resident customer
Zero-rated e-Tax invoice issued and transmitted through HomeTax with the 0% VAT rate and export-indication code
Digital service performance packet: service delivery report, access/usage logs, server logs, IP/geo-location records and other objective proof that the service was consumed outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and KCS may jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Failure to produce the required export, service-performance, or foreign-exchange documentation, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, results in reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of 10% VAT on the export proceeds, plus additional tax under the Basic Act for National Taxes: 20% of underpaid VAT for negligence and 40% for fraudulent or aggressive misreporting, together with late-payment interest charged daily. False customs declarations or false export documentation may be penalized by Korea Customs Service with administrative fines and criminal referral. Violation of the FX repatriation deadline under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is punishable by imprisonment of up to 3 years or by a fine not exceeding KRW 30,000,000, and the NTS will also disregard the zero-rating claim and claw back the VAT with penalties. The collection/assessment statute of limitations is 5 years generally and 10 years where fraud is involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank and monetary authority, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal foreign exchange policy authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree; supervision of AML/CFT obligations for reporting entities is carried out by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), with licensed domestic commercial banks acting as the designated foreign exchange bank channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized current-account regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won (KRW) is not a fully freely convertible currency in the international offshore market, but onshore current transactions such as software licensing, SaaS subscription fees, salaries, and repatriation of dividends are generally permitted if the underlying transaction is genuine and supported by documentation. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity contributions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), are subject to mandatory filing with a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA rather than unrestricted approval. Dividend remittances to foreign shareholders are permissible after the completion of statutory capital verification and corporate income tax filing, provided the foreign investor has reported its investment and the profit distribution is supported by audited financial statements and board resolutions. For an AI avatar video generation company classified as ISIC 6201 software development, the main convertibility exposure is the need to evidence outbound royalty, cloud infrastructure, and subcontractor payments with service agreements, invoices, and payment purpose codes. There is no general surrender obligation for export proceeds, and foreign-currency accounts may be maintained, but settlement through a licensed domestic bank is mandatory for administrative control. The practical hurdles are documentary, not prohibition: each cross-border remittance requires the bank to identify the business purpose and record the foreign exchange transaction code before release of KRW or foreign currency. Surplus funds cannot be converted speculatively, and foreign exchange derivatives are only permitted when a genuine underlying exposure exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be collected within 18 months from the export date under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, unless an extension is granted by the designated foreign exchange bank for justified reasons. There is no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender requirement in Korea; the receipt can be held in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account or sold for KRW at a licensed foreign exchange bank. The exporter must report the receipt transaction to the designated bank, preserve the underlying customs declaration, invoice, or service contract, and any uncollected export proceeds after the 18-month window require a delayed-collection report and a documented explanation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail and legally constrained. South Korea does not recognize the EU-style electronic money institution license; a non-bank fintech must obtain approval under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act from the Financial Services Commission to provide payment services. An offshore digital EMI without a Korean license cannot issue KRW current accounts, cannot process local foreign exchange reports, and cannot serve as the receiving bank for FIPA equity injections or dividend remittances. Global payment gateways such as Stripe and Paddle can be used only for foreign currency merchant collection and settlement of customer SaaS/AI video subscription fees, but the commercial funds must then be swept into the licensed Korean bank operating account. Any EMI representation suggesting it can replace a domestic Korean account for corporate treasury should be rejected by compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Korean Yuhan Hoesa, at least one authorized signatory, ideally the representative director or a locally resident financial officer appointed by a board resolution, must attend a physical branch interview in Korea. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for corporate accounts, especially where the company has no established Korean credit history and foreign shareholders control the entity. The bank will require verification of the corporate seal registration certificate, business registration certificate, certified articles of incorporation, and the signatory's passport or Korean alien registration card. Video KYC may supplement but cannot replace the physical interview for corporate customers under the Korean AML framework, which is stricter than the simplified onboarding available to low-risk individual accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity caused by foreign corporate shareholders and a multi-layer capitalization structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annotated group entity chart; certificates of good standing or incumbency for every shareholder in the chain; signed UBO declaration for every natural person holding 10% or more; notarized share register; passport copies and proof of address for all ultimate natural persons; certified translations of all foreign corporate registry filings and source-of-wealth documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident statutory directors and remote formation with no demonstrable local management presence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or consular-legalized board resolution appointing a local authorized agent; notarized power of attorney executed by the overseas representative director; the local agent's Korean alien registration card or passport; certified copy of the Korean corporate seal registration certificate; business registration certificate; certified articles of incorporation; and a signed undertaking to notify the bank within 14 days of any change in directors, seal, or authorized signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from high-risk jurisdictions or cryptocurrency-linked sources used for the equity subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed term sheet or subscription agreement; 6 to 12 months of bank statements from the remitting investor; corporate financial statements or legitimate fundraising evidence; complete digital asset conversion trail and blockchain transaction analysis if any cryptocurrency liquidation occurred; independent CPA capital verification report after deposit; and a director declaration confirming no predicate offense or sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Market mismatch between low local operating revenue and high expected cross-border payments for cloud infrastructure, AI model licensing, and overseas subcontractors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer agreements, subscription dashboards, and VAT invoices; cloud infrastructure contracts with AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or GPU service providers; AI model licensing agreements and IP ownership registrations; intercompany transfer pricing documentation; and accounting vouchers reconciling recognized revenue, accrued expenses, and actual disbursement beneficiaries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity funding must be remitted by the foreign investor directly from its own account to the Yuhan Hoesa's designated temporary capital deposit or ordinary KRW account at a licensed foreign exchange bank. Before remittance, the company should file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with the designated bank or KOTRA and obtain the Foreign Investment Report Certificate. Each SWIFT wire should include clear reference to the FIPA report number and use the payment purpose code for equity participation. The designated bank will verify the remitting shareholder identity against the filed foreign investment application. Upon clearing of funds, a Korean certified public accountant must issue the capital verification report, and the company must register paid-in capital with the court and transfer the working capital into the basic operational currency account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for AI video SaaS and avatar generation services is SWIFT MT103 for regular operating payments, license fees, service fees, and cloud infrastructure disbursements. The bank will require the underlying contract, invoice, and foreign exchange disbursement report before releasing funds. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are legally available but are generally unsuitable for pure digital software services; they may be used only when the transaction includes tangible deliverables such as servers, source code escrow certificates, or hardware accompanied by transport documents. For all trade settlement modes, the remitting entity must ensure the beneficiary is not a sanctioned jurisdiction and must preserve each transaction record for at least five years to satisfy KoFIU examination requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/KRW forward contracts with a documented underlying current transaction exposure, limited to the expected invoice amount and tenor of the commercial obligation
Onshore KRW non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts executed through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank for eligible trade or service exposures, strictly prohibited for speculative purposes
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only where the company has a confirmed long-term borrowing facility or material foreign capital/profit repatriation exposure exceeding one year
Long FX options purchased from a licensed Korean bank with premium-only payment and a matching underlying SaaS, license, or capital account transaction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of members and approval of audited or unaudited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Yuhan Hoesa members; corporate records kept at the registered office (no direct government filing required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unjustified failure to convene the ordinary members meeting or to prepare the required minutes exposes the managing director to a statutory negligence fine of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,700); continuing procedural dormancy may support a court petition for judicial dissolution or eventual strike-off from the corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with financial statements and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, on or before March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The NTS will issue a deemed assessment and add an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax for under-reporting plus statutory daily delinquency interest on the tax amount; repeated non-filing and non-payment can trigger asset seizure, cancellation of the business registration certificate, and administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge (local income tax) return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent municipal/provincial tax office (Si/Gun/Gu local government)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual corporate income tax return deadline; calendar-year companies file on or before April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax delinquencies attract an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid amount plus statutory interest; unresolved arrears can lead to tax seizure, suspension of business, and a final administrative strike-off for inactive and non-filing entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor report filing and public disclosure (only when the statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a mandatory-audit Yuhan Hoesa, the auditor report must be submitted before the ordinary members meeting and the audited financial statements filed with the FSS within 2 weeks after the meeting; for calendar-year companies this normally falls in March-April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or to file the audit report may result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approx. USD 37,000), fines against responsible officers, and non-approval of the annual financial statements; continued failure can lead to mandatory correction orders and strike-off from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment status report (if the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, on or before January 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can trigger a negligence fine of up to KRW 2,000,000 (approx. USD 1,500), loss of foreign-investment tax reductions and cash-grant benefits, and delisting from the foreign-invested company registration; the investor is typically required to cure the omission within a 30-day reporting period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is compulsory if the Yuhan Hoesa exceeds the asset-based threshold at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year: total assets of KRW 12 billion or more (approximately USD 9.2 million). The Korean rule does not use turnover or headcount as standalone audit triggers. A mandatory audit also applies if the company is listed, is a financial company under the relevant regulatory laws, raises securities through public solicitation, or is designated for audit by the Securities and Futures Commission for public-interest reasons. Companies below KRW 12 billion in total assets are not required to obtain a statutory external audit unless separately designated, although small companies may be audited by members as a matter of governance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS), which are converged with IFRS, are mandatory for audited public-interest companies. Non-public companies, including most Yuhan Hoesa entities, may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or K-IFRS, and eligible SMEs may apply the Korean SME Accounting Standards (K-SME GAAP). The accounting framework must produce financial statements that present true and fair value in accordance with the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and the Commercial Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation return for ordinary non-financial Yuhan Hoesa companies. Instead, the Yuhan Hoesa must keep a statutory Register of Members that identifies the beneficial owners and capital contributions, and any shareholding transfer or change in membership must be reflected in that register and approved or recorded as required by the articles of incorporation. For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) imposes a 30-day post-event reporting window: any transfer of shares, change in holding ratio, or change in foreign investor identity must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the event. At the annual members meeting, the register is confirmed for dividend entitlement and voting purposes, and the managing director must certify that the register is accurate. The statutory registers must be kept at the registered office and made available for inspection to members and to court or administrative authorities upon demand.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national Corporate Tax (CIT) plus 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on the CIT = 26.4% combined marginal rate for taxable income above KRW 300 billion; progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion.
